messages:
Sam: Hey team, escalated from CS — customer A (mobile app) sees streaming responses go quiet for ~20-30s then the client socket gets a reset. They report it happens when user moves from phone hotspot -> carrier data. Logs show 'no incoming bytes' then a TCP RST.
Ella: Thanks Sam — can you paste the client logs + request id? is this our hosted API or Dedicated? any proxy in front? :mag:
Sam: Hosted API, request id: r-8f3b2c9a. App logs snippet:
```
[2025-07-11T12:02:03Z] SSE: open
[2025-07-11T12:02:21Z] SSE: silence (no bytes for 22s)
[2025-07-11T12:02:24Z] connection: ECONNRESET from remote
```
Also mobile says keepalive interval is 30s (default), app doesn't send pings midstream.
Kevin: Hmm. Sounds like NAT mapping expiry or carrier dropping idle flows when the client changes networks. What are edge idle timeouts? ops-bot: Edge-proxy idle-timeout=20s for HTTP/TCP flows in region-us-west-2 (configured).
Nina: That matches — proxy is closing at 20s of inactivity. If client keepalive is 30s it will be vulnerable on network switches.
Ella: Customer says they see partial output (some tokens) then silence, not always a full RST immediately — jittery. Could be brief pause during TCP handoff then mapping changes and proxy closes.
Kevin: Repro idea: 1) Connect via hotspot, start stream, 2) toggle hotspot off (phone switches to carrier), 3) observe: likely 20s silence then proxy closes. Can we get pcap or android network logs? Suggest they enable a shorter keepalive (10s) or send a tiny event every 15s.
Sam: I asked CS to get a screen recording & device logs. They can reproduce consistently by walking into building -> hotspot drops, phone resumes cell in ~5s.
Nina: Short term mitigation: we can increase edge idle-timeout for that customer's tenant to 60s (needs ops sign-off). Long term: client should send application-level keepalives < edge timeout.
Ella: Also check token TTL refresh — if token rotates at the same time it could trigger EOF. But logs show no 401s.
Kevin: For engineering owners: runtime + eng-infra. Possible fixes:
- Add server-side heartbeats for active streams when no tokens rotation.
- Make edge-proxy treat established SSE streams as long-lived and use TCP-level keepalive probing.
Sam: CS asked about billing: customer worried about being charged for aborted streams. We should clarify billing behavior on token aborts/partial outputs.
Nina: Billing note: we bill on tokens produced; aborted streams that produced partial tokens are billed for produced tokens only. I'll add a note to CS.
Ella: Quick repro steps to share with customer:
1) Start stream from app (note request id)
2) Wait 10s, toggle wifi/hotspot off
3) Wait 30s and check logs for 'silence' followed by RST
4) Send client keepalive < 15s and verify continuity
Include sample curl for SSE connect (for desktop repro):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-base" --no-buffer
```
Kevin: I'll open an internal issue with tags [runtime][edge-proxy][support-escalation] and link request id r-8f3b2c9a.
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2025-9875, assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
Sam: Thanks — leaving with eng oncall. If we increase tenant idle-timeout we should coordinate with infra to avoid resource misuse. :thumbsup:
